dedupe_keys.name: tethys water demand data for the contiguous united states 1980 2100 pnnl

description: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory produced this gridded water demand dataset with the Tethys model, giving monthly withdrawals and consumption at 1/8 degree for irrigation, thermoelectric, municipal (public supply and domestic), livestock, manufacturing and mining uses, with each cell's renewable and non-renewable source share, for 1980 to 2100 under eight scenarios of human-Earth system change. It combines state sector demands from GCAM-USA, power plant siting from the CERF model, and scenario climate and population forcing. Coverage is the contiguous United States. The data are a free download through the DOE Data Explorer record and its DOI. Caveats: checked against USGS 2010-2020 water use, the totals agree within about 7 percent per sector, but the spatial allocation differs, with normalised RMSE of 68 to 171 percent for single HUC6 basins. Simulation uses: sector demand scenarios for water supply capacity planning and drought adaptation. Related records: the USGS public supply water use reanalysis (data-usgs-public-supply-water-use-reanalysis-huc12) and global gridded sectoral water use (data-global-gridded-monthly-sectoral-water-use-1971-2010).
